identity.name: link_coa_to_parcels
identity.description: LINK (the second runLinkPhase family, Spec 124 R-EG): re-matches every eligible CoA (a lead and a normalized street name) to a parcel on every run through the address cascade — the address-points bridge, then the parcels-table exact, then name-only when the street number is blank — and keeps lead_parcels' coa: rows in step with it: a guarded upsert of each CoA's link, a per-batch keyed retraction of (lead, parcel) pairs no longer derived, and one sweep of rows whose CoA vanished. A CoA whose link changed this run gets its parcel's centroid coordinates, the neighbourhood containing that centroid and parcel_linked_at on coa_applications; no other CoA is written (operator rulings 2026-10-18, wave-4 plan question 10).

why_lock.text: Spec 42 §6.8 Phase D allocation, ported from the legacy `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 4201` (link-coa-to-parcels.js:48); recorded in src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts.

write_discipline.scope: lead_id LIKE 'coa:%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM coa_applications ca WHERE ca.lead_id = lead_parcels.lead_id)

why.text: The legacy guarded upsert (link-coa-to-parcels.js:458-470, pinned L11): ON CONFLICT (lead_id, parcel_id), rewritten only when match_type or confidence moved; matched_at is the run clock and is never a guard (LG-9), so matched_at = this run's clock means exactly 'this link was inserted or changed this run' — the signal the back-fill (writes[2]) keys on. The scope is the vanished-lead sweep's (retract "departed", Spec 124 R-EG (5)): after the loop, ONE statement deletes the coa: rows whose CoA no longer exists and whose lead no row of this run derived — the legacy ghost cleanup (:585-600, LCTP-D6), now one statement instead of a LIMIT 1000 loop; every lead_parcels write and retraction carries lead_id LIKE 'coa:%' because the permit mirror trigger trg_mirror_permit_parcels_to_lead_parcels (migrations/144_*.sql:66) co-writes the table with permit: rows (LCTP-D9).

guard_why.text: LG-24 precedent (link_parcels writes[1], link_massing writes[2]): no IS DISTINCT FROM guard applies to a DELETE. The scope IS the guard: the statement touches only coa: rows of THIS batch's leads whose (lead_id, parcel_id) is not among the pairs this batch just derived (the compute's NOT_DERIVED fragment, shared with the before-image SELECT so the two cannot drift). The target itself is operator-ruled: wave-4 plan question 10 (y 2026-10-18), ruling 1 — 'link_full_retraction of departed (lead, parcel) pairs'. Grandfathered in scripts/steps/_schema/grandfathered.json.

guard_columns_why.text: LG-9 escape hatch, moot here (the link_massing writes[2] form): guard is "none", so guard_columns is never consulted, and no run-clock column is declared on this target.

write_discipline.scope: lead_id = ANY(this batch's leads) AND lead_id LIKE 'coa:%' AND (lead_id, parcel_id) NOT IN (this batch's derived pairs)

why.text: Ruling 1 (LCTP-D3/D6): re-check every run means a CoA whose match moved to another parcel, or that no longer matches any parcel, loses the old pair — the legacy write-once step kept it forever (pinned L11). Fires after the guarded upsert and the back-fill, inside the same batch transaction (runner executeKeyedLinkWrites); its rows are read once first (stale_link_select_sql) for the R-M / LG-17 before-image and for the leads that lost a pair. Counted on written.e2 (deleted). The empty-source guards (parcels, address_points, parcel_address_points) stop the run before any write when a matching input is empty, so an empty input can never read as 'every link departed'.

guard_columns_why.text: LG-9 escape hatch, declared on purpose: the legacy back-fill guarded the same four columns, parcel_linked_at (= the run clock) included (link-coa-to-parcels.js:532-546, pinned L12), so every CoA the statement reaches is written and its marker moves. The narrowing is the scope (only a CoA whose link changed this run), not the value guard; with the clock in the guard the statement writes exactly the rows the scope selects, which is the marker's 'link changed at' meaning that enrich_parcels reads (scripts/lib/compute/enrich-parcels.js:1122-1123).

write_discipline.scope: id of a CoA in this batch whose link changed this run: it lost a (lead, parcel) pair, or its lead_parcels row was inserted or rewritten at this run's clock

idempotent_rerun_why.text: A second run over an unchanged corpus derives the same links: the upsert guard leaves matched_at alone and no pair departs, so no CoA is in scope and the back-fill writes 0 rows.

why.text: Ruling 1 (LCTP-D7, operator y 2026-10-18): the coa_applications back-fill (latitude, longitude, neighbourhood_id, parcel_linked_at = the run clock) fires ONLY for a CoA whose link changed this run. link_coa writes the same coordinates from the linked permit (scripts/link-coa.js:660-680; 26,723 of 29,627 parcel-linked CoAs carry them, assessment §1.4), so an unconditional back-fill under re-check-every-run would rewrite them on every run and the two steps would fight. The neighbourhood is the one whose polygon contains the parcel centroid (ST_Contains, PostGIS only — the Turf path is retired, R-W, LCTP-D5; NULL when none, never -1); a CoA that lost its link and gained none keeps its coordinates and neighbourhood (no parcel to take them from; the legacy step never cleared them) and only its marker moves. The R-EG (4) link-change statement, bound to lost_keys, batch_keys, run_at; set_source compute (LG-22). Counted on written.e3.

invalidates.when: Ruling 1 (the link_parcels O4 row 7 copy, operator y 2026-10-18): every eligible CoA is re-matched on every run (staleness.mode_select none), so a CoA whose parcel or address changes is re-linked by the next run and its marker moves then; there is no write-once filter left to go stale (LCTP-D3). The same re-derive keeps lead_parcels' coa: rows current: changed links are rewritten (guarded upsert), pairs no longer derived are retracted per batch, and rows of vanished CoAs are swept (R-EG (5)).

why.text: Three write statements per batch inside ONE batch transaction (runner executeKeyedLinkWrites): the guarded upsert (e1), the link-change back-fill on coa_applications (e3) and the keyed DELETE of pairs no longer derived (e2); the back-fill and the delete are issued every batch (an empty set writes nothing). Plus ONE vanished-lead sweep after the loop (e1 retract departed, R-EG (5)), before-imaged. The match queries, the cumulative coverage query and the stale-pair SELECT are reads.

Ruling 3 (LCTP-D5, R-W 124a:137): the neighbourhood lookup, the centroid-outside-polygon count and the bridge's parcel-area tie-break are PostGIS; the Turf / JS point-in-polygon fallback is retired, so a database without PostGIS fails before any read instead of taking a second code path (link_parcels precedent, scripts/link-parcels.descriptor.json).

relrowsecurity = true on lead_parcels with 0 policies (assessment §1.4, read-only DB): under a non-bypass role every write affects 0 rows with no error and the counters read 0 (Spec 124 R-CT; trap 2).
relrowsecurity = true on coa_applications with 0 policies (assessment §1.4): the back-fill would affect 0 rows with no error (Spec 124 R-CT; trap 2).

on_row_error_why.text: Ruling 2 (LCTP-D4, operator y 2026-10-18; a declared deviation, R-BD): per-row SAVEPOINT isolation is retired. The runner owns the batch transaction; one bad row fails the batch and the step, with its key in the error. 0 per_row_errors in the last legacy runs (1497, 1547).

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a counter or a coverage scalar the runner already measured in the same run; a check that throws is a compute defect and must redden the run.

why.text: The corpus floor is stated on its complement (coa_corpus_unlinked_pct <= t; a bound cannot be 100 − x); the slice decision is declared once (unmatched_coa_pct). There is no no-work lane: every eligible CoA is walked every run, and audit_table.phase follows sharing.varies_by_chain.phase (4, the chain index; LCTP-D8, the O1 fleet standard). The two bridge type counters (tier_1a_type_confirmed / tier_1a_type_tolerant) are carried, restored on the bundled RE-FREEZE night (Spec 124 R-ID): classifyMatches counts them per batch and the runner sums them (extra_counters).

limitations.what: lead_parcels is co-written by the trigger trg_mirror_permit_parcels_to_lead_parcels on permit_parcels (migrations/144_*.sql:66; 245,270 permit: rows), i.e. by converted link_parcels. This step never touches a permit: row (every statement is scoped lead_id LIKE 'coa:%'), but the table has two writers (LCTP-D9; R-BC (c) for coa owes the writer declaration).

The first converted run re-matches every eligible CoA (about 33,800): the 3,773 stamped-but-unlinked CoAs are the upper bound for new links, and departed-pair retractions are unknown until the night-P4 POST measures them.

recovery.reset: Re-run the step: every run re-derives every eligible CoA's link, rewrites only the links that changed, retracts the pairs no longer derived and sweeps vanished leads, so a plain re-run IS the repair. TRUNCATE is never correct (the table carries permit: rows).

interrupted_why.text: Every run re-derives every eligible CoA (staleness.mode_select none), so there is no incremental mode for a crash to be followed by; each batch's upsert, back-fill and keyed delete commit together, and a run killed mid-loop leaves earlier batches committed and the next run's full re-derive repairs the rest (the link_massing form).

why.text: The legacy records_total = processed (:652): the eligible CoAs walked this run (the runner's R-EG (1) processed counter).
New lead_parcels links inserted this run (the legacy reported 0; declared diff — the runner counts inserts and updates apart).
Existing links whose match_type or confidence moved (the legacy reported every match; declared diff).
Every eligible CoA was re-matched and every bound held.
The run completed and a WARN bound (unlinked corpus, unmatched share, neighbourhood coverage, centroid outside polygon, missing normalized names) fired. Row-derived.
parcels, address_points or parcel_address_points is empty: the run stops before any write, so an empty input never reads as every link having departed.
PostGIS is missing (ruling 3) or an rls_bypass_or_policy precondition is not met (R-CT).
A declared logic variable resolved absent or outside its [min, max] under on_invalid fail, above the lock (the legacy zod refusal, pinned L1).
A batch statement threw (ruling 2, fail_fast): the batch transaction rolls back whole, earlier batches stay committed, and the error names the failing statement.
Advisory lock 4201 held elsewhere: no SQL inside the lock and a row-derived SKIP summary (pinned L17).
